Chapter 245-0242: Heavenly King Andy Lau Joins Hainei

The finals for the second "Sanguosha National University League" had been moved from winter break to summer break.

Therefore, the qualifying rounds began in the spring of this year, with online matches held on the two days of each weekend.

Last year's finals were held in Beijing; this year, they were moved to Magic City.

Moreover, the date was set for the day after the ChinaJoy electronics exhibition ended.

The contestants and audience for the "Sanguosha" finals could arrive in Magic City two or three days early and catch the CJ exhibition as well.

The event was scheduled for late July.

"For this year's CJ exhibition, I plan to make a bigger splash for Youke," Qu Guohao said.

Chen Guiliang asked, "Besides Sanguosha cosplay, what other activities are you thinking of?"

Qu Guohao said, "We'll directly hire a bunch of beautiful showgirls locally in Magic City. It's really hot this year, so a row of showgirls in crop tops and ultra-short hot pants, handing out flyers in front of our booth. Absolutely eye-catching! And it won't cost much, much cheaper than bringing staff over from Beijing."

"That could work." Chen Guiliang couldn't help but smile; he enjoyed seeing that kind of scene too.

Showgirls at the CJ exhibition only appeared last year. Everyone discovered they were cheap and effective, so this year all the major game companies were planning to do it.

The operator for "Voyage Century" was even going to hire foreign models as showgirls this year. How could the old lechers of this era withstand such a test? They would stop and stare for a long time even if they didn't play "Voyage Century".

Entering July, Huang Xinyuan began recruiting the SP team.

There was quite a bit of big news this month.

First, Britain's Prince Harry partied hard at a nightclub and was caught by his girlfriend, a scandal known worldwide. Then, General Kim ordered the launch of several missiles into the sea near Japan, and Japan declared it would retaliate with missiles.

Over in the United States, twenty thousand female interns flooded Washington, D.C. They wore mini-skirts that barely covered their butts and tight, sleeveless tops, teetering on high heels as they served tea, poured water, and photocopied documents in various departments.

This was a yearly summer tradition, but this year the number of interns was particularly high, and their attire had become increasingly revealing. It was already making the old American officials in D.C. uncomfortable, so reporters flocked to cover it, and even Chinese newspapers reprinted the stories.

Every one of them wanted to be Monica Lewinsky, trying to replicate Zippergate.

Over in Britain, a super-mom had given birth to a child every year for 20 consecutive years. This year, at 48, not only did she stop having children, but she also abandoned her husband and kids for an online romance, running away to be with her internet lover.

This was the biggest news story in Britain this year, shattering the worldview of countless British people.

The Middle East was at it again.

Saddam Hussein wasn't dead yet, but he had been on a hunger strike in prison for 10 days.

A major tsunami in the South China Sea.

A Turkish plane crash.

Amidst all the various news in July, the most sensational story in China was the Baidu layoffs.

"Damn, this is causing a huge uproar. Just how bad are Baidu's relations within the industry!" Chen Guiliang was utterly shocked as he read.

Sohu, Sina, Tencent, Tom.com, HC360, Yesky, Xinhuanet, CCIDnet, Yangcheng Evening News, Southern Metropolis Daily, Information Times, Guangzhou Daily, Business Information Daily, The Beijing News... nearly a hundred websites and print media outlets collectively launched a crusade against Baidu.

Xie Yang looked at the news. "Baidu's a tall tree that catches the wind. It's obvious someone is coordinating this behind the scenes. But they really deserve it this time. Baidu went too far."

Who was coordinating it?

No idea.

But there was no doubt it was Sohu that fired the first shot.

The two internet giants, Baidu and Sohu, thus began an unprecedented war of words.

They exposed each other's dirty laundry, went for the jugular, determined to beat each other's brains out.

It's normal for a company to have layoffs, but to be attacked by a mob like this was really because Baidu was being inhumane.

Some Baidu employees in Beijing, Magic City, and Pengcheng were suddenly told to complete their termination procedures and get out within four hours, without any prior notice.

It was simply outrageous.

In fact, Baidu had started doing this two or three months prior, it just hadn't blown up back then.

One of the employees, named Mu Yifei, had already applied for labor arbitration. He was inexplicably laid off two months ago, and his Baidu stock options, worth over a million yuan, were voided. Baidu offered no compensation whatsoever!

Chen Guiliang still wasn't quite accustomed to this era.

He was shocked by the rampant infringement in the color ringtone industry, and now he was shocked by Baidu's completely unreasonable layoffs.

Building a society ruled by law was truly a long and arduous journey.

"Mr. Chen, 'Crazy Stone' has been released. The shot with you and your friend is about 1.5 seconds long. You also have a facial close-up," Ning Hao sent a text.

Chen Guiliang texted back, asking, "Are there any screenings near Peking University?"

Ning Hao replied, "Huaxing International Cineplex, Haidian Theater, and Zhongguancun Cinema have screenings. But you can only watch it in the morning and afternoon, not in the evening."

Chen Guiliang didn't know whether to laugh or cry.

The students were already home for summer vacation, and office workers had no free time during the day. The screening times for "Crazy Stone" were ridiculous. Who were they showing it to? Ghosts?

New directors had no rights.

He would have to wait until the film's word-of-mouth improved before the theaters would give it normal screening times.

Damn it, this was my screen debut.

Chen Guiliang logged into his Xiaonei and Hainei accounts and posted a blog entry: "'Crazy Stone' is out, and I have a 1.5-second cameo in it. Who can find me?"

Then, he posted a mobile Weibo message.

The comment sections of his posts on each account quickly filled with messages.

"Great Hero Chen actually became an actor!"

"Chen Ten-billion, with your net worth, why not spend a little more to be the male lead?"

"Haha, only a 1.5-second shot. Did you offend the director, Mr. Chen?"

"You have the nerve to post about a 1.5-second clip?"

Most of the comments were teasing, mainly because the screen time was so absurd.

Of course, some were also asking where they could watch the movie.

Ning Hao quickly got the news and called, "Mr. Chen, thank you so much for helping with the promotion! If you need anything in the future, just say the word. I promise I'll be there whenever you call."

But Chen Guiliang had other intentions. "Didn't Andy Lau invest in this film? He should be promoting it more."

Ning Hao said, "Heavenly King Liu has helped with promotion too. But he's a very busy man and can't spare much time. He can only give it a mention when he's talking to the media."

"Have Andy Lau register a Hainei account. I'll help promote his account, I guarantee he'll have tens of thousands of followers in a day," Chen Guiliang revealed his true motive. "Then, Andy Lau can promote the movie through Hainei."

"This..."

Ning Hao paused for a moment. "I'll try."

Andy Lau was at home studying the script for "Protégé," which was scheduled to start filming next week.

After receiving Ning Hao's call and understanding the reason, Andy Lau said, "I only know how to type on a computer and send and receive emails. I don't know how to use any other computer tools."

"Uh... how about I give you ByteDance's CEO Chen's phone number? You two can discuss it over the phone," Ning Hao said. "Mr. Chen is a really nice person. He's still a student at Peking University, but he's already worth over 1 billion. Plus, he comes from a rural background and built everything himself from scratch. This time, he even took the initiative to help us promote the movie."

Andy Lau was surprised. "That impressive? A student can earn a net worth of 1 billion."

Ning Hao said, "The 1 billion net worth is just his shares in one company. He has another gaming company that's also extremely profitable. You can even play its game in Hong Kong."

"Then send me his phone number," Andy Lau said.

Andy Lau was an investor in "Crazy Stone," and it was part of his "Focus: First Cuts" project.

He didn't have to show up in person, just post a message online to promote it. In principle and in practice, he had no reason to refuse.

Besides, after hearing Ning Hao's description, Andy Lau was also very curious about Chen Guiliang.

A moment later, Andy Lau sat in front of his computer and called Chen Guiliang. "Mr. Chen, hello, this is Andy Lau."

"Hello, Heavenly King Liu," Chen Guiliang was ecstatic. "Calling me Mr. Chen is too formal, just call me Xiao Chen. In terms of age, you're my senior."

Andy Lau chuckled, "Won't that make me sound too old?"

"Not at all, you've always been very young," Chen Guiliang said.

After some small talk, Chen Guiliang said, "First, open your browser and type in the Hainei website address... Let me read it to you."

In those days, you could access mainland websites from Hong Kong.

But it was very slow.

After Andy Lau entered the URL, he waited quite a while before finally seeing the Hainei homepage.

"In the top right corner of the webpage, there's a 'Login/Register' option..."

Chen Guiliang meticulously taught Andy Lau how to register and then guided him through experiencing the various features. But he couldn't add funds from Hong Kong, so for the time being, Andy Lau could only use the free items.

The mobile Weibo feature couldn't even be activated; Andy Lau would need to go through the relevant application process first.

Chen Guiliang said, "I'll deposit 500 yuan for you. You can use it to buy paint to brush your house, buy wallpaper, furniture, a TV, and so on... In the bottom left of your personal homepage, there's a 'My Home.' That's your little online nest."

Andy Lau was usually very busy and almost never went online. His understanding of the internet was limited to sending and receiving emails.

At this moment, Chen Guiliang had already verified him as a "Big V" and deposited 500 yuan into his account.

He also put up an urgent promotion on the Hainei homepage, directly posting a banner: "A Warm Welcome to Asian Heavenly King Andy Lau on Hainei!"

Andy Lau?

The first to be alerted were the entertainment reporters who regularly lurked on Hainei for celebrity news. They didn't just stake out Hainei, but also the entertainment channels of other portal websites and the celebrity blogs on the three major blog platforms.

Now they had news to write about. Andy Lau joining Hainei was enough for an article.

Andy Lau himself was completely unaware of this; he was busy decorating his house. There were over 20 different styles for the house's exterior. Andy Lau chose a big villa, which cost money, and then started decorating the interior, having a great time.

He had completely forgotten about promoting "Crazy Stone."

Chen Guiliang waited very patiently, logging into Sanguosha to play a game in the meantime.

During his final exams, he had been writing his book like mad. The fifth volume of "Those Things in the Ming Dynasty" was finished. Now he finally didn't have to worry about how to answer to Li Xunhuan.

A full 40 minutes passed before Andy Lau called again. "My house is decorated. What else can I do?"

Chen Guiliang then guided him to farm vegetables, steal parking spots, open a shop... all were mini-games made by Youke.

These mini-games were non-exclusively licensed to ByteDance and were available for users to play on Xiaonei and Hainei. At the same time, they could also be played on Youke's platform.

Andy Lau played enthusiastically for a good while before finally remembering the real purpose. "How do I promote the movie?"

Chen Guiliang said, "Go back to your personal homepage. At the top, you'll see your follower count. Go to your journal page, and you can write a blog entry. All your followers will receive a notification about your new entry. You can also attach pictures to your posts. There's also a photo album feature where you can upload photos you've taken..."

Andy Lau glanced at it and said in surprise, "It's only been a little over an hour, right? I already have over 60,000 followers?"

"Haha, you're a Heavenly King, after all," Chen Guiliang laughed. "I helped promote you on the website's homepage, so a lot of users saw the news and came to follow you."

Andy Lau thought about it carefully and was even more shocked. "This method of promotion is so fast and convenient. I type a few dozen words and post it, and tens of thousands of fans receive it."

Chen Guiliang pressed his advantage. "Why don't you invite all your old friends from Hong Kong to join? It doesn't matter if they don't know how to use it. I'll give you the number for one of our staff members. Mainland users really like Hong Kong celebrities. As long as they join Hainei, they can interact with their fans, which will help their careers on the mainland. Hainei's registered user base is about to break 10 million."

"That many?" Andy Lau genuinely began to consider inviting his friends to register.

Especially those friends who weren't doing so well. After the collapse of the Hong Kong film market, many celebrities had no work and no income. If he could bring them to Hainei, once their follower counts grew, it might be a new path for them.

Chen Guiliang said, "I'll send you the office number for a Hainei staff member."

Andy Lau said, "I'll see what I can do. A lot of my old friends are like me, they don't know how to use computers. Some don't even know how to send or receive emails."

"They'll learn after being taught once," Chen Guiliang said. "I'll have the staff teach them step by step."

This was a huge win!

(End of this chapter)
